newsitem.title: UK: Tanker rates steady, Suezmax higher on good interes.
newsitem.headline: Tanker rates steady, Suezmax higher on good interes.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates generally held at last week's levels but enquiries for Suezmax vessels from West Africa raised rates for one-million tonne business, brokers said.

A spate of fixtures for 125,000 and 130,000 tonne cargoes from West Africa for both eastern and western destinations helped to lift Suezmax rates elsewhere. Sun chartered the Knock Muir from West Africa to the U.S. Atlantic Coast at W97.5, up from W95 last week.
"There are a lot of enquiries in West Africa. We have seen a lot of fixtures on one million barrels in various areas, including the Med," a Med broker said.

There were eight Suezmax fixtures and one VLCC booked from West Africa, mostly to the U.S. Gulf and the U.S. Atlantic Coast at rates ranging from W63.75 for the VLCC to W100 for a 130,000 tonne cargo. Two cargoes were booked into the Far East but neither rate was reported.
Cross-Med rates were steady with Suezmax vessels hard to come by. Brokers put levels at W90 for old tonnage and W100 for modern vessels.
VLCC rates from the Middle East to Japan held at last week's higher levels of W67.5 while cargoes heading West saw rates steady at W55 for the transatlantic voyage.
"Across the board it is holding and we do not expect rates to move much over the next couple of weeks," a European broker said.
In the U.K./Cont market, rates were still depressed for Aframax vessels. Brokers put rates at W95 with the possibility of achieving W97.5 from some ports.
